title: The ~112 built-in functions are invisible in the editor: no autocomplete, signature help, or hover docs
existing_state: The Scintilla autocomplete provider (Services/Editor/ScriptAutocompleteProvider.cs) completes step commands (lines 116-161), top-level keys (163-178), required option keys (180-217), built-in symbols like _output/_prompt (92-104, 219-231), and host columns — but not one of the ~112 scripting functions (grep for regex_match/date_add/base64/ip_in_cidr across the file: zero matches). The Flow Canvas property panels are equally function-blind (same grep over FlowCanvas/src: zero matches). FunctionRegistry exposes RegisteredNames (Services/Scripting/FunctionRegistry.cs:90) but nothing consumes it, and it only covers 71 of the functions anyway — 20 legacy functions live in a hardcoded switch (Services/Scripting/JsonUtilities.cs:347-564) and the json.* family is a third dispatch path, so the registry under-reports the surface by ~40%. The registry stores only name→delegate (FunctionRegistry.cs:25); there is no arity/description/category metadata to drive tooling. Today a user writing `- set: x = ...` must memorize function names or keep SCRIPTING.md open.
recommendation: Add a metadata layer to FunctionRegistry (signature string, one-line description, category) populated at registration in each IFunctionCategory.Register, plus a static table covering the 20 legacy JsonUtilities names and the json.* methods so one API enumerates the full surface. Then wire ScriptAutocompleteProvider to offer function completions with signature hints when the caret is in an expression position (after `set: x = `, inside if:/while:/assert: conditions), reusing its existing description-dictionary pattern (BuiltInSymbolDescriptions at line 219). Expose the same list to Flow Canvas property panels via the bridge for a function-picker/hint in expression fields. The same unified table powers the function-name lint in UX-010.
user_benefit: Script authors stop alt-tabbing to SCRIPTING.md and stop guessing names like index_of vs indexof. This is table-stakes IDE behavior for what is now a full scripting language.

evidence.note: Completes commands/keys/symbols; zero function names anywhere in the 1246-line file (verified by grep)
Name→delegate dictionary only; RegisteredNames exists but is unconsumed and misses legacy + json.* names
20 legacy functions (length, list, trim, upper, lower, replace, split, join, substring, sort, ...) dispatched outside the registry

mockup_idea: Side-by-side editor screenshot: before — user types 'set: x = reg' and gets nothing; after — popup listing regex_match(text, pattern[, group]), regex_match_all(text, pattern), regex_replace(text, pattern, repl) each with a one-line description, and a calltip showing the signature after '(' is typed.
